title: Dedicated capacity loadproof telemetry validator and customer acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Objective: build a reproducible, telemetry-driven load testing harness and a customer-facing acceptance protocol that proves Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees across tenant variability and autoscaler interactions. Scope: harness components (workload generator, deterministic replay, tenant-mixing), realtime telemetry collectors (per-tenant QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit ratio, batching efficiency, GPU utilization), benchmarking methodology, and a checklist for customer signoff runs. Out of scope for this ticket: long-term reporting UI work and billing integration (tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Lab harness can execute a deterministic 60-minute ramp-and-sustain profile with tenant-mix config files and produce a signed artifact (JSON+tgz) with golden metrics. 2) Benchmark runs include tail-latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99) and token-cost estimates; p99 must meet configured SLOs for the customer tier or a documented exception. 3) Autoscaler safety test shows no SLA violations when scaling actions trigger under synthetic burst scenarios. 4) Acceptance runbook and one-page summary exported to Drive and linked from customer onboarding checklist.
test_plan_summary: - Generate tenant mixes from anonymized production traces (synthesized to remove PII). - Provide three canonical profiles: steady-state high-throughput, microburst (10x QPS for 30s), and tail-heavy session synthesis (long sequences). - For each profile run: capture per-tenant latency quantiles, batching sizes, KV cache hit ratio, GPU occupancy, request requeues, and any fallback model routing events. - Repeat runs with autoscaler throttled/delayed to validate safety margins. - Produce a CI artifact and run tag for auditability.
harness_architecture: Components: workload-generator (dockerized, config-driven, supports deterministic seeds), replay-transformer for converting prod traces into tenant-mixes, collector agents (Prometheus exporters + a lightweight log artifact writer), and an orchestration harness (k8s job-based runner) that snapshots environment, pins model versions, and records node allocation. The harness includes a deterministic-seed mode so identical runs can be compared across fleets.
telemetry_metrics: Primary metrics: total tokens/sec, per-tenant QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency (in ms), token-per-second-per-GPU, average KV cache hit ratio, batching efficiency (tokens per batch), GPU SM utilization, OOM/retry counts, autoscaler decisions (scale-up/scale-down events and timestamp), and model-fallback occurrences. Each metric must be exported to Prometheus and included in the artifact as CSV and summary JSON.
benchmark_protocol: Protocol: 1) baseline warmup 10 minutes, 2) ramp to target QPS over 5 minutes, 3) sustain at target for 30 minutes, 4) microburst injection (where applicable), 5) cooldown 10 minutes. For each run compute: steady-state mean token throughput, p99 latency during sustain window, tail-latency slope (difference between p95 and p99), and cost-per-token estimate using current runtime billing model. Run each profile 3 times; median of metrics is used for acceptance.
customer_acceptance_checklist: - Pre-run: confirm model-version pin, region, and Dedicated pool name; collect customer workload representative files. - Run: execute harness with deterministic-seed and tenant-mix provided by customer/Prod-synth team. - Post-run: generate artifact, upload to Drive, run dashboard snapshot link, and produce one-page summary with pass/fail and signed metrics. - Signoff: Customer (or SE) confirms results meet documented SLOs or accepts documented mitigations. - Archive: move artifacts to /redwood-dedicated/acceptance/ with run-id tag.
decisions: Use deterministic-seed replay by default to enable regression comparisons
Prometheus exporters + artifact JSON will be canonical storage for run data
Include autoscaler-failure-injection scenarios as mandatory for P0 customers
risks: Synthetic tenant mixes may not fully capture customer variability leading to false positives
Autoscaler chaos tests could cause transient errors that require careful communication to customers
Resource contention in shared lab clusters may mask true Dedicated behavior; isolated pools are preferred
blockers: Provisioning isolated Dedicated lab pools (infra ticket INF-2418)
Access to sanitized production traces from telemetry team (data-privacy signoff)
Small missing k8s ServiceAccount permissions for the harness runner (security review)
